incident-bot: ALERT: streaming frontends p99 latency breach in us-west-2. Metric=p99_response_time value=5.9s threshold=2.0s severity=sev2. Routing tag=hosted/sse

alex (sre-oncall): i'm paged, taking incident. seeing p99 jump to ~6s across streaming endpoints. p95 elevated to ~600-900ms. No high 5xx rate, just long pauses where clients see no chunks for many seconds.

rita (eng-runtime): loading traces. link: https://grafana.redwood/streaming?panel=p99_tail

rita (eng-runtime): traces show many requests with repeated small writes then long idle gaps. Runtime chunk queue grows, worker threads blocked on socket write/backpressure. Some nginx upstream logs show `upstream timed out` and `proxy_send_low_watermark` warnings.

alex (sre-oncall): customer impact: tori, any support tickets?

tori (prod-support): yup — multiple customers report "streaming transcription stalls, resumed later". Affected sessions ~2.8% in us-west. No cancellations but bad UX. I've prepared a short note to send once we have a mitigation.

sam (eng-platform): checking ingress. Found spike in 499s following long stalls and some TCP retransmits. Proxy config shows default `proxy_buffering on; proxy_read_timeout 60s; send_timeout 60s;`. Could be buffering + short timeouts + slow readers.

alex (sre-oncall): hypotheses: (A) proxy buffering + short timeouts cause head-of-line when a client stops reading; (B) certain client versions incorrectly coalesce reads and cause the server to backlog; (C) autoscaler ignores long-lived idle connections so capacity looks fine but handlers are saturated.

incident-bot: Created IR-1823551234. Runbook: streaming-slow-consumers.

alex (sre-oncall): immediate mitigations to try (in order):
1) disable proxy buffering for /v1/stream and /chat/streaming routes (`proxy_buffering off; proxy_request_buffering off;`)
2) bump `proxy_read_timeout` and `send_timeout` to 600s for streaming paths
3) deploy canary to 10% of frontends in us-west and measure p99
4) identify top source IPs / user-agents with longest idle gaps and temporarily terminate connections if idle > 30s of no reads
5) provide customers an opt-in websocket path or short-poll fallback if available

rita (eng-runtime): i can flip proxy_buffering off on a canary pool and add `proxy_request_buffering off; proxy_read_timeout 600s;` Will also add a quick metric for `connection_idle_write_seconds` on runtime to spot slow readers.

sam (eng-platform): i'll prepare canary rollout and a traffic-split to route 10% to canary. also adding a temporary routing policy to prefer us-east for new sessions if capacity permits.

deploy-bot: deploy job `canary/nginx/sse/us-west-2` queued by rita (eng-runtime) at 1823551360

rita (eng-runtime): applied to 3 canary nodes. monitoring now.

alex (sre-oncall): early signal: canary p99 dropped from 5.9s -> 1.6s, p95 back to ~210ms. good sign.

sam (eng-platform): rolling config to all frontends in us-west-2 with safe concurrency. increasing timeouts and disabling buffering for streaming routes.

deploy-bot: deploy job `rollout/nginx/sse/us-west-2` started by sam (eng-platform) at 1823551454

rita (eng-runtime): after full rollout p99 is ~1.8s, p95 ~230ms. client stall reports down from ~2.8% -> 0.3%. 499 spikes normalized.

tori (prod-support): sending update to affected customers: "We've applied a fix that reduces stream stalls in US-West-2. If you still see issues please send session ids and user-agent."

alex (sre-oncall): root cause analysis notes for postmortem: chain of factors — nginx/proxy default buffering + relatively short timeouts + a subset of slow-reader clients that read in big, infrequent bursts. That caused server write buffers to fill and head-of-line blocking in the chunking pipeline. Autoscaler didn't react because connections are low CPU but hold worker resources.

rita (eng-runtime): follow-ups:
- T-2001: add runtime metric `idle-bytes-since-last-write` and alert on high slow-reader count
- T-2002: implement proactive slow-consumer detection to throttle or requeue streams (drop or background them)
- T-2003: server-side SSE reconnect token so clients can resume without redoing work

sam (eng-platform): follow-ups:
- T-2004: add nginx streaming config test to CI to prevent accidental buffering for streaming paths
- T-2005: consider autoscaler rule to count long-lived connections and scale out based on connection backlog, not CPU alone

tori (prod-support): follow-up: email customers with summary and link to postmortem once available.

alex (sre-oncall): severity downgraded to P3. IR-1823551234 closing notes: mitigated by disabling proxy buffering and increasing read/send timeouts. Canaries looked good. Total impact window ~2h, ~2.8% sessions affected in region, no data loss. Postmortem to be filed with assigned tickets.

incident-bot: IR-1823551234 status RESOLVED at 1823551780"
